a: 2 types of data verification can be used: proof reading and double entry. Proof reading refers to where the user manually reads the data entered into a field, to ensure it is accurately entered and correct. It relies on a human to double check if it's right, and there is a possibility they may miss an error. It is also slow therefore making it not very effective. Another method is (continued on extra sheet) double entry, which refers to a user entering the same data in 2 fields, of which a computer checks if both fields match e.g. a password box. This method is more effective, since no human is involved in checking the correctness of the data leading to less errors. It is much faster and accurate too.
note: Quality of written communication assessed; middle band. Both methods described and some evaluation, but the key limitation is missing: verification only checks the data matches the source, so if the original data is wrong (or the same mistake is typed twice) it is still accepted. Finish with a clear judgement.

a: Client-side processing refers to where some parts of data are locally processed and executed through various languages such as JavaScript, such as updating the basket of which the user wishes to purchase. It is better since it reduces the server load, and the output is saved immediately to the server and client for fast access. Server-sided processing refers to where data is executed on a server hosting the web page application, of which more sensitive data that shouldn't be tampered with is processed on, such as the payment process, of which it shouldn't be processed client sided as the user could freely alter the value of the purchase to a lower value. The data processed on the server is kept on the server, and some parts are sent back to the client e.g. the confirmation order.
note: Quality of written communication assessed; bottom band.
